story.head: The Blues come in hot
paras: The Islanders (11-7-5) lost 4-2 to Toronto on Monday, while the Blues have won four straight. Going in, the Blues are fifth in the Central (tied for 14th in the NHL) and the Isles fourth in the Metropolitan (tied for 16th).
The Blues’ record (.583) is about what their chances are worth. The Islanders’ record (.587) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.501), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Blues ice the puck less than anyone (1st), keep things calm after the whistle (lowest) and take a lot of high-quality shots (2nd). As for the Islanders, they roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st), have had some of the best goaltending in the league (1st) and get their defensemen shooting (2nd). The Blues keep dangerous shots away, but the Islanders give up a lot of them.

Robert Thomas (5 G / 19 A / 24 P in 24 GP) leads the Blues in scoring, with ten points in his last five games. Mason McTavish (8 G / 6 A / 14 P in 24 GP) has a team-high eight goals. For the Islanders, Matthew Schaefer (9 G / 17 A / 26 P in 23 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Simon Holmström (10 G / 8 A / 18 P in 23 GP) has a team-high ten goals.

Joel Hofer (10-6-1 / .920 SV% in 17 GS) has been outstanding for St. Louis and is expected to start. Ilya Sorokin (9-5-2 / .917 SV% in 16 GS) has been terrific for the Islanders and is expected to start.
